note: ROOT-RULINGS R-2/R-5: with no usable perl (a perl on PATH older than 5.28: a stand-in that runs this host's perl with STORE_TEST_PERL_V=5.026003; the launcher checks no version, main.pl's guard runs the launcher's fallback for a hook (the path the launcher's hook wrapper hands it), stdin unread; the stand-in counts its starts, one per hook, and refuses anything else), hook PreCompact prints nothing, exits 0 and appends one helper_runtime_missing row (the launcher's shell fallback: under the default ~/.local/state/<plugin>/handoffs/.watch, STATE-ROOT, or $XDG_STATE_HOME/<plugin>/handoffs/.watch while handoff_root is the default and XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute path, and nothing under ~/.claude/handoffs); any other subcommand prints REFUSED: helper-runtime and exits 3. 0.1.4 T-15: the fallback writes its row only under an absolute folder that no folder from it up to / holds a .git (folder or file: a git work tree) or a .planning folder, and with no .planning part (also one not made yet, any letter case); the walk runs on the path as given and from its deepest existing folder read through symlinks (cd -P); a root in a git work tree (also through a symlink), a relative root and a .planning root get no row and no folder, the hook still exits 0 with nothing on stdout; a log_dir that is not an absolute path (root-invalid in the helper) gets no row, which would land under the hook's working folder; such a handoff_root with log_dir unset sends the row to the default folder, as the helper's logs go (0.1.4 review F-4(g)) (an exec step sets those roots: the runner's home guard refuses a root env value that is not absolute) 0.1.4 review F-1: a hook's perl runs as the launcher's child, so a perl that is found but cannot start (an interpreter line that points nowhere, a version manager's shim with no perl picked: it ends with 1 to 128) takes the same fallback: exit 0, nothing printed, one row, under /bin/sh, dash and bash. 0.1.4 F-1 follow-up: a hook's perl that ends on a signal (an exit above 128: ABRT, as a perl that aborts on a missing library, or SEGV) takes the same fallback, exit 0 and its row; the payload's session id when perl ended before reading stdin, unknown when it had read it

steps.name: the stand-in perl is started once for the hook (no version-check spawn)
the default root under an absolute XDG_STATE_HOME
a handoff_root equal to the default reads under XDG_STATE_HOME too
a relative XDG_STATE_HOME is ignored
an explicit other handoff_root stays the root
a relative handoff_root is root-invalid: with log_dir unset the row goes to the default folder (as the helper; here under an absolute XDG_STATE_HOME), nothing under the hook's working folder
exec: cd "$1" || exit 9; printf '{"session_id":"%s","cwd":"%s","hook_event_name":"PreCompact","trigger":"auto"}' "$2" "$1" | env $3 "$0" hook PreCompact; echo "rc=$?"; find . | LC_ALL=C sort

steps.name: a relative log_dir: no row either
exec: cd "$1" || exit 9; printf '{"session_id":"%s","cwd":"%s","hook_event_name":"PreCompact","trigger":"auto"}' "$2" "$1" | env $3 "$0" hook PreCompact; echo "rc=$?"; find . | LC_ALL=C sort

steps.name: a drive-form handoff_root (not absolute outside Git Bash's perl): the row goes to the default folder too
exec: cd "$1" || exit 9; printf '{"session_id":"%s","cwd":"%s","hook_event_name":"PreCompact","trigger":"auto"}' "$2" "$1" | env $3 "$0" hook PreCompact; echo "rc=$?"; find . | LC_ALL=C sort

steps.name: with an absolute log_dir beside a relative handoff_root the row is written there
exec: cd "$1" || exit 9; printf '{"session_id":"%s","cwd":"%s","hook_event_name":"PreCompact","trigger":"auto"}' "$2" "$1" | env $3 "$0" hook PreCompact; echo "rc=$?"; find . | LC_ALL=C sort

steps.name: a handoff_root inside a git work tree: no row, nothing made (T-15)
a log_dir in a linked worktree (a .git file): no row
a log_dir reached through a symlink into a git work tree: no row (read through cd -P)
a log_dir under a git work tree whose folder links out of it: no row (the path as given is walked too)

a relative handoff_root (read against the cwd, whose first folder exists there): nothing under it, the row in the default folder; set by a shell in the case's work folder, since the runner's guard refuses a relative folder option it passes itself
a handoff_root inside a .planning folder: no row
a handoff_root under a .Planning part not made yet (any letter case): no row
a handoff_root in a folder that holds a .planning folder (a project's own state beside it): no row
begin
a perl on PATH that is found but cannot start (its interpreter line points nowhere): the hook still exits 0, prints nothing and writes its row (0.1.4 review F-1)
the same under /bin/sh, dash and bash (each one found)
exec: for s in /bin/sh dash bash; do p=$(command -v "$s") || continue; d="$1/logs-${s##*/}"; printf '{"session_id":"%s","hook_event_name":"PreCompact","trigger":"auto"}' "$2" | CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_LOG_DIR=$d "$p" "$0" hook PreCompact >"$1/out" 2>&1; rc=$?; n=$(grep -c helper_runtime_missing "$d/$2.classic.jsonl" 2>/dev/null); echo "${s##*/} rc=$rc rows=${n:-0} out=$(wc -c <"$1/out" | tr -d ' ')"; done

steps.name: a version manager's shim with no perl picked (it starts, complains and exits 126): exit 0, nothing printed, the row

setup.script: echo 'No version is set for command perl' >&2; exit 126

steps.name: a perl that ends on a signal before it reads stdin (TERM and KILL: an abort on a missing library or a crash, ABRT or SEGV, takes the same exit-above-128 path, but on macOS those make ReportCrash write into the real ~/Library/Logs, outside the test's HOME) under /bin/sh and dash (when found): exit 0, nothing on stdout, the row with the payload's session id (0.1.4 F-1 follow-up)
exec: for s in /bin/sh dash; do p=$(command -v "$s") || continue; for g in TERM KILL; do d="$1/sig-${s##*/}-$g"; printf '{"session_id":"%s","hook_event_name":"PreCompact","trigger":"auto"}' "$2" | STORE_TEST_SIG=$g CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_LOG_DIR=$d "$p" "$0" hook PreCompact >"$1/out" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; n=$(grep -c '"ev":"helper_runtime_missing"' "$d/$2.classic.jsonl" 2>/dev/null); echo "${s##*/} $g rc=$rc rows=${n:-0} out=$(wc -c <"$1/out" | tr -d ' ')"; done; done

steps.name: a perl that ends on a signal after it read stdin: exit 0, nothing on stdout, the row under the unknown session id
